rabbitmq/durable-quarantine.detail: candidate-01 configuration effect on the pinned Dapr RabbitMQ component, not a harness or verifier defect
rabbitmq/durable-quarantine.mechanism: The previous vector restarted the broker (docker restart) and recreated only the consumer. The publisher sidecar found its AMQP channel closed on the next publish. The pinned component waits reconnectWait (2 s) before reconnecting but returns when the request context ends (rabbitmq.go:321-328). The 500 ms outbound timeout always ends it first, so no attempt ever reconnects: Dapr resiliency outbound timeout 500 ms x 3 attempts + 2 x 200 ms backoff = 1.9 s, then HTTP 500 "context deadline exceeded". The vector never exercised its guarantee; the harness then waited 45 s for an effect that could not arrive.

rabbitmq/secret-rotation.detail: code-level in the pinned Dapr RabbitMQ component; candidate-01 knobs are inapplicable
rabbitmq/secret-rotation.mechanism: After delete_user, the stale publisher sees its channel closed. The only call that could return the broker's ACCESS_REFUSED is the reconnect dial, but it runs only after reconnectWait and its error is discarded (`_ = r.reconnect(...)`, rabbitmq.go:328). Under candidate-01 the dial never runs (Dapr resiliency outbound timeout 500 ms x 3 attempts + 2 x 200 ms backoff = 1.9 s); with any admitted value its error still cannot become the publish error. The 500 carries "context deadline exceeded", which attributable_denial correctly rejects.

rabbitmq/cancellation-backpressure.detail: code-level in the pinned Dapr RabbitMQ component (upstream negative-confirm fix unreleased per the 2026-11-10 record; not re-checked in this offline slice)
rabbitmq/cancellation-backpressure.mechanism: The effective reject-publish/max-length-4 policy was measured. All eight publishes returned 204 while the publisher logged three failed confirmations; the pinned publishSync logs the NACK and returns nil (rabbitmq.go:290-299), so the broker rejection becomes HTTP 204 and three acknowledged IDs are absent at the bound.

rabbitmq/missing-bindings.detail: code-level in the pinned Dapr RabbitMQ component
rabbitmq/missing-bindings.mechanism: Binding absence is physically measured before and after the unbound publish, beside a passing bound control. The component publishes with mandatory=false (rabbitmq.go:282), so the broker confirms the unroutable message and Dapr returns 204.

kafka/cancellation-backpressure.detail: two independent failing predicates; only the harness defect is fixed (EventStore c4b90c42); the vector still fails

mechanism.acknowledgedLoss: The harness creates the pressure topic with retention.ms=60000 and segment.ms=1000 and keeps its consumer stopped through six throttled publishes plus native diagnostics. The two 204 records (offsets 0-1, 00:09:59.33) sat 65 s unconsumed; Kafka deleted segment 0 for a 60000 ms retention breach at 00:10:59.820, 4.5 s before the consumer restarted at 00:11:04.29. The group had no committed backpressure offset, so it began at the advanced log start.
mechanism.negativeConfirmRejected: Produce byte-rate quotas throttle and never reject. Each over-quota publish ran 3 x 3 s Dapr timeouts + 2 x 200 ms = 9.40 s and returned 500 "context deadline exceeded", while all three attempts were later appended (log end 20 = 2 + 6 x 3). The only accepted Kafka rejection, "kafka server: The throttling quota has been exceeded", is not produced by this fault.
